medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (1 mg) by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Seen 01/12/2026.

Three months at alprazolam 1.5 mg at bedtime. Sleep a little lighter in the first two weeks after the reduction, then settled. Using CBT-I techniques (fixed wake time, getting out of bed when not sleeping). No rebound anxiety, no tremor or palpitations. GAD-7 6. A stressful fall with nosebleeds and a transfusion, handled well.

Plan: reduce to 1 mg at bedtime (1 mg tablet) starting tonight. Continue therapy, now every two weeks. Next step in about three months.
Outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: Nasal Laser Coagulation
documents.author: ENT
documents.body:
Procedure: laser coagulation of anterior septal telangiectasias, bilateral, in office.
Indication: HHT epistaxis.
Anesthesia: topical lidocaine with oxymetazoline pledgets.
Findings: multiple small telangiectasias of the anterior septum bilaterally, right more than left, as at consultation.
Technique: under endoscopic guidance, lesions treated with low-power laser in a circumferential pattern from the periphery inward, avoiding the central vessel. Minimal bleeding, controlled with a pledget. No packing.
Patient tolerated well. Instructions: saline gel three times daily for two weeks, humidifier, no nose blowing for a week, expect crusting. Follow-up 6 weeks.
Otolaryngology

documents.title: After ENT procedure
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI ENT did the laser Tuesday. Lots of crusting and a tiny bit of pink on the tissue, nothing like a real nosebleed. They said that's expected. Just keeping you in the loop.

documents.title: RE: After ENT procedure
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for the update, Paula. That sounds like normal healing. Keep up the gel. Call ENT or us if you get a bleed that doesn't stop with 20 minutes of pressure.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Seen 02/17/2026.

After ferric carboxymaltose in November and ENT laser treatment in January, she reports one or two short nosebleeds a week. Energy good.

Labs today: hemoglobin 12.1, ferritin 74.

Assessment: iron deficiency anemia from HHT bleeding, currently corrected.
Plan: continue oral iron. CBC and ferritin every 3 months at her PCP's lab (next in May); repeat IV iron if ferritin falls below 50 or hemoglobin drops. Antihistamine premedication for any future transfusion. Return in 6 months or sooner if counts fall.

Hematology

documents.title: Otolaryngology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: ENT
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski. Seen 02/24/2026, six weeks after laser coagulation of anterior septal telangiectasias.

Nosebleeds have dropped to one or two brief episodes a week. Endoscopy: treated areas healed with mild crusting, no active bleeding, no perforation.
Plan: continue saline gel and humidification. Repeat laser treatment as needed if frequency increases; return in 6 months or sooner.
Otolaryngology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
47F, 6-month follow-up. Doing well. Nosebleeds 1-2/week, short, since ENT laser in January. Energy good. Hematology letter 2/19 reviewed: Hgb 12.1, ferritin 74; next labs May here.

Alprazolam now 1 mg qhs (psychiatry taper, next step April). Sleep ok most nights with CBT-I. RLS rare. PD unchanged, neurology in April. Periods minimal.

Meds: carbidopa-levodopa 25-100 TID; alprazolam 1 mg qhs; ferrous sulfate 325 daily; loratadine prn; LNG-IUD (5/2024).
Allergies: NKDA; shellfish (hives); packed red blood cells (hives - premedicate); tree pollen, dust mites.
PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 5.

Exam: well, good color. Lip/tongue telangiectasias. RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema. Neuro nonfocal, no tremor.

A/P:
- HHT/IDA: stable after IV iron + ENT laser. CBC/ferritin in May (standing order).
- GAD, insomnia: improving, taper per psychiatry.
- PD, RLS: stable.
- HM: up to date. Flu/COVID done in Sept.
RTC physical in fall.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy faxed refill request for alprazolam 1 mg addressed to PCP. Per PCP, psychiatry is managing the taper and prescribes it. Called pharmacy to redirect to psychiatry; called pt, she has 10 days left and will message psychiatry today. She confirmed she knows not to run out.

documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Seen 04/13/2026.

Tolerated the step to 1 mg without withdrawal symptoms; sleep holding with CBT-I. GAD-7 5. Mood good.

Outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Seen 04/21/2026.

Parkinson disease remains stable on carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 three times daily, nine years from diagnosis, without fluctuations, dyskinesia, falls or hallucinations. Restless legs are much quieter now that her iron is replete; she rarely has symptoms. Alprazolam being tapered by psychiatry, now 0.5 mg at bedtime.

Exam on medication: normal speech, expression and tone; no tremor; finger and foot taps normal; gait normal with good arm swing; pull test negative.

Plan: no changes. Prescription renewed. Return in 12 months.
Outside neurology

documents.title: Lab result note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 12.4, ferritin 61 - stable, above hematology's threshold of 50. Copy to hematology. Next draw August. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Summer check-in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: School's out in two weeks. Nosebleeds still about once a week and short. Do I need anything before the summer? And can my August blood draw be done anytime that month?

documents.title: RE: Summer check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Paula, nothing needed before summer. The standing order for your CBC and iron is good any time in mid to late August; no fasting needed. Enjoy the break.

documents.title: Physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Could I book my physical for after school starts, a Tuesday afternoon in late September?

documents.title: RE: Physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're booked for your annual physical Tuesday 9/22 at 3:30. Flu and COVID vaccines can be given that day.
